---
title: "PLSC 40601"
subtitle: "Advanced Topics in Causal Inference · University of Chicago · Spring 2026"
---

This is a graduate-level course considering modern advances in causal inference and experimental design. In particular, we will consider how machine learning methods can be leveraged to address causal questions. We will read a selection of papers introducing and implementing techniques and research designs, with applications to the social and health sciences and public policy.

We will discuss what these new methods are able to offer, and where they may have limitations. The course will be oriented around class discussion and student presentations on the readings.

An introductory course in probability and statistics is required; this prerequisite can be met by courses in statistics, biostatistics, economics, political science, sociology, or related fields. Coursework in causal inference is recommended but not required; additional reading references will be provided for students who have not had prior exposure to causal inference methodology.

## Schedule

1.  [Week 1. Causal inference, identification, and course orientation](./weeks/01-course-orientation.qmd) What changes once the causal question is already defined and machine learning is brought in as part of estimation, inference, and decision-making?
2.  [Week 2. Adjustment under selection on observables](./weeks/02-adjustment.qmd) How should machine learning be used when identification rests on unconfoundedness and the core challenge is nuisance estimation under high-dimensional covariates?
3.  [Week 3. Heterogeneous treatment effects](./weeks/03-heterogeneity.qmd) What kind of individualized causal object do you actually want to estimate: a CATE surface, a ranking over units, or an actionable rule?
4.  [Week 4. Representation learning for causal inference](./weeks/04-representation-learning.qmd) When is it useful to learn a representation of the covariates rather than estimate effects directly in the observed feature space?
5.  [Week 5. When ignorability fails: proxies and instruments](./weeks/05-proxies-instruments.qmd) What can you do once selection on observables is no longer plausible and you need either proxies for latent confounding or instruments for treatment variation?
6.  [Week 6. Policy learning and evaluation](./weeks/06-policy-learning.qmd) Once you can estimate heterogeneity, how do you turn it into treatment decisions and evaluate those decisions with observational or logged data?
7.  [Week 7. Efficient estimation: DR, DML, and TMLE](./weeks/07-efficient-estimation.qmd) How do influence functions, orthogonal scores, and cross-fitting organize the modern efficient-estimation toolbox?
8.  [Week 8. Generalizability, transportability, and policy shift](./weeks/08-transportability.qmd) Why does an internally valid causal estimate or learned policy not automatically transport to a new population, site, or deployment regime?
9.  [Week 9. AI-assisted measurement and valid inference](./weeks/09-ai-measurement.qmd) How can model-generated labels improve measurement without being mistaken for ground truth?
